cards.definition: **Definition.** The useful application payload completed per declared interval after protocol overhead retransmission duplication and discarded work.
major_error_concepts: Calling TCP payload bytes application goodput when application framing rejects some data.
cards.prompt: Define Application goodput. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The useful application payload completed per declared interval after protocol overhead retransmission duplication and discarded work.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The bits required in flight to occupy a specified path at a target rate and round-trip time.

cards.prompt: Define Bandwidth-delay product. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The bits required in flight to occupy a specified path at a target rate and round-trip time.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The minimum effective service capacity along a specified path for a specified traffic class and interval.

cards.prompt: Define Bottleneck service rate. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The minimum effective service capacity along a specified path for a specified traffic class and interval.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified fields and local state selecting the receiving protocol instance endpoint or application.
major_error_concepts: Choosing a process from destination port alone without host or binding context.
cards.prompt: Define Demultiplexing key. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specified fields and local state selecting the receiving protocol instance endpoint or application.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered addition and interpretation of protocol metadata around a higher-layer unit at send and receive boundaries.

cards.prompt: Define Encapsulation and decapsulation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ordered addition and interpretation of protocol metadata around a higher-layer unit at send and receive boundaries.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified sender receiver client server peer intermediary or router responsibility at one protocol layer and instant.
major_error_concepts: Calling one host permanently client at every layer and direction.
cards.prompt: Define Endpoint role. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specified sender receiver client server peer intermediary or router responsibility at one protocol layer and instant.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The interface through which one protocol consumes a lower service while preserving separate peer semantics and implementation state.
major_error_concepts: Drawing stacked boxes and transferring reliability or security across every boundary.
cards.prompt: Define Layer service boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The interface through which one protocol consumes a lower service while preserving separate peer semantics and implementation state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The maximum specified bit-transfer rate of one link under the named layer and coding boundary rather than an end-to-end completion rate.
major_error_concepts: Calling advertised line rate application goodput.
cards.prompt: Define Link bandwidth. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The maximum specified bit-transfer rate of one link under the named layer and coding boundary rather than an end-to-end completion rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The separate absence late-order and repeated-delivery observations relative to a measured sequence and vantage.
major_error_concepts: Calling every gap loss immediately or every retransmission proof of original loss.
cards.prompt: Define Loss reorder and duplication state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The separate absence late-order and repeated-delivery observations relative to a measured sequence and vantage.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The interface direction clock capture mechanism sampling and visibility boundary governing what one trace can establish.
major_error_concepts: Treating one host capture as a complete path ground truth.
cards.prompt: Define Network observation vantage. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The interface direction clock capture mechanism sampling and visibility boundary governing what one trace can establish.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The division of an application byte or message sequence into transport and network units under framing MTU and protocol rules.
major_error_concepts: Calling one application write one packet or one TCP segment permanently.
cards.prompt: Define Packetization boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The division of an application byte or message sequence into transport and network units under framing MTU and protocol rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The node-local interval for parsing lookup validation scheduling or protocol work under a configured implementation and load.
major_error_concepts: Calling all nonpropagation delay queueing.
cards.prompt: Define Processing delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The node-local interval for parsing lookup validation scheduling or protocol work under a configured implementation and load.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The travel time implied by path length and signal propagation speed independent of packet length.
major_error_concepts: Using link bandwidth to compute propagation delay.
cards.prompt: Define Propagation delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The travel time implied by path length and signal propagation speed independent of packet length.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned message grammar endpoint roles state transitions timers errors extensibility rules and normative requirements governing peer communication.
major_error_concepts: Calling a port number or implementation name the protocol contract.
cards.prompt: Define Protocol contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned message grammar endpoint roles state transitions timers errors extensibility rules and normative requirements governing peer communication.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The version-qualified header fields and payload exchanged between peers at one layer with exact length and interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Calling every observed unit a packet and losing which protocol owns its fields.
cards.prompt: Define Protocol data unit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The version-qualified header fields and payload exchanged between peers at one layer with exact length and interpretation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The waiting time before service at a bottleneck determined by arrival order queue state scheduler and service rate.
major_error_concepts: Using average utilization alone to claim an exact per-packet wait.
cards.prompt: Define Queueing delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The waiting time before service at a bottleneck determined by arrival order queue state scheduler and service rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An observed-rate contract specifies the transferred quantity, successful-completion rule, observation interval, population, and direction used to compute a rate.
major_error_concepts: Dividing unlike quantities or measurements from different intervals and calling the result throughput.
cards.prompt: Define observed-rate contract. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An observed-rate contract specifies the transferred quantity, successful-completion rule, observation interval, population, and direction used to compute a rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The time required to place a specified number of bits on a link at a configured line rate.
major_error_concepts: Dividing bytes by bits per second or including propagation distance twice.
cards.prompt: Define Serialization delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The time required to place a specified number of bits on a link at a configured line rate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The joined transmission propagation processing and queue timeline across specified hops and forwarding behavior.
major_error_concepts: Adding incompatible one-way RTT and per-link quantities or skipping repeated serialization.
cards.prompt: Define Store-and-forward path delay. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The joined transmission propagation processing and queue timeline across specified hops and forwarding behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The completed transferred bits or units divided by a declared observation interval population and direction.
major_error_concepts: Calling the smallest link rate observed throughput without a transfer measurement.
cards.prompt: Define Throughput. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The completed transferred bits or units divided by a declared observation interval population and direction.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The time-qualified IPv4 protocol-to-link binding with origin reachability and expiry state used for local frame construction.
major_error_concepts: Calling cached ARP permanent authority or end-to-end reachability proof.
cards.prompt: Define ARP cache entry. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The time-qualified IPv4 protocol-to-link binding with origin reachability and expiry state used for local frame construction.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv4 local-link exchange asking for a protocol-address binding and returning a claimed link address under cache and trust qualifications.
major_error_concepts: Sending ARP to a remote subnet host rather than the next hop.
cards.prompt: Define ARP request and reply. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv4 local-link exchange asking for a protocol-address binding and returning a claimed link address under cache and trust qualifications.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The set of interfaces receiving a specified link broadcast absent filtering segmentation or routing boundaries.
major_error_concepts: Calling every switched network one broadcast domain regardless of segmentation.
cards.prompt: Define Broadcast domain. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The set of interfaces receiving a specified link broadcast absent filtering segmentation or routing boundaries.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The frame-delivery distinction between one link destination and all members of a broadcast domain under switch behavior.
major_error_concepts: Forwarding a link broadcast through routers by default.
cards.prompt: Define Ethernet unicast and broadcast scope. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The frame-delivery distinction between one link destination and all members of a broadcast domain under switch behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message is an ICMPv6 control message interpreted under Neighbor Discovery type, code, option, source, destination, hop-limit, and link-scope validation rules.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting an ICMPv6 type without enforcing Neighbor Discovery link-scope and message-validation rules.
cards.prompt: Define IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message is an ICMPv6 control message interpreted under Neighbor Discovery type, code, option, source, destination, hop-limit, and link-scope validation rules.

cards.definition: An IPv6 solicited-node multicast address is the link-local multicast address obtained by appending the target unicast or anycast address low-order 24 bits to ff02::1:ff00:0/104. Neighbor Solicitation uses the corresponding group for address resolution, rather than an IPv4-style broadcast. Different addresses sharing those low bits share the group, so group membership is not a unique host identity.
major_error_concepts: Using all target bits as an IPv6 broadcast destination.
Assuming different IPv6 addresses always have different solicited-node multicast groups.
cards.prompt: Define IPv6 solicited-node multicast. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Construct the address from ff02::1:ff00:0/104 plus the target low 24 bits.
It narrows on-link solicitation scope but is not broadcast or a globally unique host identifier.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The time-qualified mapping from observed source link addresses to ingress ports used for later forwarding decisions.
major_error_concepts: Learning destinations from destination fields or keeping stale movement forever.
cards.prompt: Define Learning-switch table. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The time-qualified mapping from observed source link addresses to ingress ports used for later forwarding decisions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local-link identifier used for delivery on one link and resolved or configured under that link protocol.
major_error_concepts: Treating a MAC-like value as global host identity.
cards.prompt: Define Link address. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local-link identifier used for delivery on one link and resolved or configured under that link protocol.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The link-local corruption-detection field and validation boundary that can reject a frame without providing end-to-end correctness.
major_error_concepts: Calling a valid link check proof that transport or application bytes are correct everywhere.
cards.prompt: Define Link integrity check. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The link-local corruption-detection field and validation boundary that can reject a frame without providing end-to-end correctness.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local-link protocol unit carrying addressing type length integrity and payload fields under one link contract.
major_error_concepts: Using final remote host link address across routed hops.
cards.prompt: Define Link-layer frame. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local-link protocol unit carrying addressing type length integrity and payload fields under one link contract.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The maximum network-layer unit accepted on one interface under a configured link configuration and encapsulation.
major_error_concepts: Subtracting Ethernet-visible frame header from an already stated IP MTU twice.
cards.prompt: Define Link MTU. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The maximum network-layer unit accepted on one interface under a configured link configuration and encapsulation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv6 response or announcement carrying target and link information with solicited override and router flags affecting cache state.
major_error_concepts: Calling every advertisement authoritative or equivalent to a router advertisement.
cards.prompt: Define Neighbor Advertisement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv6 response or announcement carrying target and link information with solicited override and router flags affecting cache state.

cards.definition: RFC 4861 neighbor-cache reachability uses five conceptual states: INCOMPLETE (address resolution pending), REACHABLE (recent positive confirmation), STALE (confirmation expired), DELAY (briefly waiting for upper-layer confirmation after use), and PROBE (sending unicast reachability probes). STALE does not mean the cached address is unusable. After probe failure the conceptual entry is discarded; implementations may expose extra labels such as FAILED, which should be identified as local extensions.
major_error_concepts: Treating STALE as an unusable mapping that cannot be used to send a packet.
Claiming FAILED is a sixth mandatory state in the RFC 4861 conceptual machine.
cards.prompt: Define Neighbor-cache reachability state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Distinguish the five RFC states INCOMPLETE, REACHABLE, STALE, DELAY and PROBE and their reachability/resolution roles.
STALE remains usable while reachability is checked; extra implementation failure labels are not additional required RFC states.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message used for address resolution reachability or duplicate-address contexts with source and target rules.
major_error_concepts: Using it to query arbitrary off-link addresses directly.
cards.prompt: Define Neighbor Solicitation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv6 Neighbor Discovery message used for address resolution reachability or duplicate-address contexts with source and target rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The host or router attachment with link protocol addresses MTU operational state queues and counters under one observation boundary.
major_error_concepts: Calling an interface a permanent physical port or one IP address.
cards.prompt: Define Network interface. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The host or router attachment with link protocol addresses MTU operational state queues and counters under one observation boundary.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The forwarding decision that retains the remote network destination while addressing the local frame to an on-link gateway.
major_error_concepts: Replacing destination IP with gateway IP in the forwarded packet.
cards.prompt: Define Off-link next-hop delivery. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The forwarding decision that retains the remote network destination while addressing the local frame to an on-link gateway.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The IPv6 host-router messages supplying default-router prefix and configuration context separately from neighbor address resolution.
major_error_concepts: Calling router advertisement a DNS answer or universal authenticated configuration.
cards.prompt: Define Router Solicitation and Advertisement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The IPv6 host-router messages supplying default-router prefix and configuration context separately from neighbor address resolution.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The local replication of a frame when the switch lacks a usable destination entry with ingress exclusion and scope rules.
major_error_concepts: Calling flooding routing or proof that every recipient accepts the payload.
cards.prompt: Define Unknown-unicast flooding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local replication of a frame when the switch lacks a usable destination entry with ingress exclusion and scope rules.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The protocol-visible loss delay rate and retransmission variation on a wireless hop without claiming physical-layer cause.
major_error_concepts: Inferring interference source or channel capacity from one application slowdown.
cards.prompt: Define Wireless-link variability boundary. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The protocol-visible loss delay rate and retransmission variation on a wireless hop without claiming physical-layer cause.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The replacement of contiguous aligned more-specific prefixes by a covering prefix only when routing and policy permit the broader advertisement.
major_error_concepts: Combining nonaligned ranges or assuming reachability for every address in the cover.
cards.prompt: Define CIDR aggregation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The replacement of contiguous aligned more-specific prefixes by a covering prefix only when routing and policy permit the broader advertisement.

major_error_concepts: Treating control-plane topology as the packet's direct forwarding instructions.
cards.prompt: Define Forwarding-table action. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The data-plane operation applying selected route interface next hop header updates MTU and policy results to one packet.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The versioned error message containing enough invoking-packet context to associate a network failure with a flow while obeying generation limits.
major_error_concepts: Treating an ICMP source address as proof of the exact failed link.
cards.prompt: Define ICMP error quotation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned error message containing enough invoking-packet context to associate a network failure with a flow while obeying generation limits.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The error generated for hop-limit exhaustion or reassembly timeout under version-specific rules and observation limits.
major_error_concepts: Calling no reply proof that no router exists at that hop.
cards.prompt: Define ICMP time exceeded. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The error generated for hop-limit exhaustion or reassembly timeout under version-specific rules and observation limits.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The 32-bit address plus prefix-length set membership used for interface and route context without classful assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Using dotted-decimal visual similarity instead of prefix bits.
cards.prompt: Define IPv4 address and prefix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The 32-bit address plus prefix-length set membership used for interface and route context without classful assumptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The version-specific division of a datagram into offset-aligned fragments with identification flags and destination reassembly under MTU constraints.
major_error_concepts: Splitting total bytes evenly without header or eight-byte offset rules.
cards.prompt: Define IPv4 fragmentation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The version-specific division of a datagram into offset-aligned fragments with identification flags and destination reassembly under MTU constraints.

cards.prompt: Define IPv4 header checksum. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The one's-complement integrity check over the IPv4 header that routers update when mutable header fields change.

cards.prompt: Define IPv6 address and prefix. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The 128-bit address and prefix set with compression syntax separated from actual bits and scope.

required_concepts: The endpoint use of a Fragment extension header while routers do not fragment ordinary forwarded IPv6 packets.

required_concepts: The forwarding selection of the matching destination prefix with greatest length before later tie-breaking.

cards.prompt: Define NAT mapping state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The middlebox translation between internal and external endpoint tuples with direction timers and filtering behavior under one implementation.

major_error_concepts: Accepting arbitrary unauthenticated MTU values forever or changing link MTU itself.
cards.prompt: Define Packet-too-big feedback. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ICMP signal carrying a constraining MTU so an endpoint can adjust packet size under validation and state rules.

required_concepts: The endpoint's time-qualified bound on packet size along a path and protocol context inferred from messages probes and loss behavior.

cards.prompt: Define Private-address scope. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The designated non-global IPv4 address space whose routing treatment and uniqueness are local-policy matters.

cards.prompt: Define Recursive next-hop resolution. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

required_concepts: The destination prefix next-hop or direct-delivery action outgoing interface metric source preference and lifecycle state considered by forwarding.

cards.prompt: Define TTL and hop-limit transition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The per-forwarding-node decrement preventing indefinite circulation and triggering version-specific discard and error behavior at exhaustion.

cards.prompt: Define Autonomous system. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The routing-policy domain identified for interdomain exchange without implying one organization topology or trust boundary universally.

major_error_concepts: Adding A's stale destination estimate twice or mixing rounds.
cards.prompt: Define Bellman-Ford routing update. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local minimization over neighbor cost plus advertised destination estimate under a recorded message round.

major_error_concepts: Choosing the shortest AS path before a higher-priority local policy.
cards.prompt: Define BGP path attributes. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The versioned origin AS path next hop preference and other properties carried or assigned for route selection and policy.

cards.prompt: Define BGP selection and export policy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The local choice among accepted paths and neighbor-specific announcement rules reflecting relationships and safety constraints.

major_error_concepts: Calling iBGP an intradomain shortest-path protocol.
cards.prompt: Define BGP session role. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The eBGP or iBGP relationship carrying path-vector information under transport policy and propagation rules.

cards.prompt: Define BGP update and withdrawal. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The incremental advertisement or removal of reachable prefixes and path attributes over an established session.

cards.prompt: Define Count-to-infinity behavior. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The gradual increase of distance-vector estimates for an unreachable destination under limited local knowledge.

major_error_concepts: Giving every node the global graph while calling it distance vector.
cards.prompt: Define Distance-vector state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The per-destination local cost and next-hop estimates learned through neighbors rather than a complete topology map.

required_concepts: The versioned statement of one router's adjacencies or network links with sequence age scope and flooding behavior.

cards.prompt: Define Link-state database. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The router's time-qualified collection of accepted advertisements from which a topology view is constructed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specified vertices links directions capacities or costs and failure state over which one routing algorithm reasons.

cards.prompt: Define Network topology graph. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specified vertices links directions capacities or costs and failure state over which one routing algorithm reasons.

major_error_concepts: Calling receipt of one hello a full synchronized adjacency.

required_concepts: The introductory neighbor state and database-exchange relationship required before routing information is fully synchronized.

cards.prompt: Define OSPF route calculation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The introductory derivation of intra-area routes from an accepted link-state database and local interface state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The distinction between learning or selecting paths and applying installed data-plane actions to packets.
major_error_concepts: Calling a routing update proof that the next packet takes that path.
cards.prompt: Define Routing and forwarding separation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The distinction between learning or selecting paths and applying installed data-plane actions to packets.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The protocol-specific additive or ordered value used in path computation and separated from business policy and measured application quality.
major_error_concepts: Calling the lowest metric universally fastest cheapest or preferred by BGP.
cards.prompt: Define Routing metric. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The protocol-specific additive or ordered value used in path computation and separated from business policy and measured application quality.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The source-rooted result of a specified graph and metric used to derive next hops with tie handling.
major_error_concepts: Selecting edges greedily by smallest individual weight without path totals.
cards.prompt: Define Shortest-path tree. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The source-rooted result of a specified graph and metric used to derive next hops with tie handling.

cards.definition: In distance-vector routing, simple split horizon omits a route from advertisements back toward the neighbor or interface from which that route was learned. Split horizon with poisoned reverse advertises that route back with an unreachable/infinite metric instead. This avoids selected two-router feedback loops, but does not establish universal loop freedom or immediate convergence; larger loops can remain.
major_error_concepts: Reversing which strategy omits the route and which advertises an unreachable metric.
Claiming either rule proves all distance-vector loops impossible.
cards.prompt: Define Split horizon and poison reverse. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Split horizon suppresses the learned route back toward its source; poisoned reverse instead advertises it there as unreachable.
The mitigation is neighbor/interface-specific and does not eliminate all larger loops or convergence delay.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The circular next-hop state during asynchronous convergence that can forward packets repeatedly until hop limit expires.
major_error_concepts: Calling every control-plane cycle a persistent topology loop without state evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Transient routing loop. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The circular next-hop state during asynchronous convergence that can forward packets repeatedly until hop limit expires.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The receiver credit limiting how much sequence space the sender may have outstanding for buffer protection separate from congestion control.
major_error_concepts: Calling the receive window the congestion window.
cards.prompt: Define Advertised receive window. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The receiver credit limiting how much sequence space the sender may have outstanding for buffer protection separate from congestion control.

major_error_concepts: Acknowledging the highest byte seen and skipping a gap.
cards.prompt: Define Cumulative acknowledgment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The receiver statement of the next contiguous sequence expected rather than proof every later observed byte is durable or application-processed.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The receiver-held byte intervals beyond a gap with overlap duplicate and capacity handling under one implementation contract.

cards.prompt: Define Out-of-order receive buffer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.

cards.definition: Under RFC 6298, a TCP retransmission timeout is computed as RTO=SRTT+max(G,4*RTTVAR), with clock granularity G; the RFC recommends rounding computed values below one second up to one second. Before an RTT sample, it recommends an initial RTO of one second or a more conservative value. A retransmission timeout backs the timer off by doubling RTO, subject to the specified bounds. Expiration triggers recovery but does not prove the receiver received no data: an ACK may have been delayed or lost.
major_error_concepts: Setting RTO equal to SRTT while ignoring variation and granularity.
Treating timeout as certain evidence that the receiver observed no bytes.
cards.prompt: Under RFC 6298, how is TCP RTO computed and backed off, and what does expiration fail to prove?

Timeout recovery includes exponential backoff, and a timeout is not proof of data nonarrival.

cards.definition: For the first valid RTT sample R, RFC 6298 initializes SRTT=R and RTTVAR=R/2. For a later valid sample Rnew, first set RTTVAR=(1-beta)*old_RTTVAR+beta*abs(old_SRTT-Rnew), then SRTT=(1-alpha)*old_SRTT+alpha*Rnew, with recommended alpha=1/8 and beta=1/4. The variation update uses the old SRTT, not its newly updated value. Samples must satisfy the RTT-measurement rules, including avoiding ambiguous retransmission samples unless the ambiguity is resolved.
major_error_concepts: Updating SRTT first and then using the new SRTT in the variation residual.
Using an unqualified RTT sample from an ambiguously retransmitted segment.
cards.prompt: Give the RFC 6298 SRTT/RTTVAR initialization and subsequent update equations, including which SRTT appears in the variation residual.
required_concepts: First sample initializes SRTT=R and RTTVAR=R/2.
Later updates use beta=1/4 on absolute deviation from old SRTT and alpha=1/8 on SRTT; preserve the stated update order and valid-sample condition.
